note: Copies of one bank alert across mailboxes (and within one, after a reconnect). A v4 txn_ingested may carry dedupe {message_id, bank_ref}: 32 lower-case hex digits each (message_id is the first 16 bytes of SHA-256 over the RFC 5322 Message-ID, angle brackets dropped, ASCII lower-cased). A certain copy (a dedupe key already in byDedupeKey on a live row) merges at once: the copy whose gates say ar pass and sender trusted wins, else the earlier one; the other gets merged_into, merge_kind certain and merge_op, leaves the live indexes, and becomes an alias on the canonical row. Re-ingesting a merged copy's ingest id is a duplicate_ingest. A probable copy (no shared key; both mailbox rows at time precision with the same bank, amount_minor, currency, direction, last4 and merchant after ASCII lower-casing and white-space folding, at most 600000 ms apart) gets copy_of the earliest live match and stays out of money until txn_copy_resolved {other_txn_id, decision: merge | keep_both | null}. A transfer notice (gates.template dib.transfer.v1 or dib.money-transfer.v1) and an account alert (dib.account.v1) of one bank, both mailbox debits at time precision with the same amount_minor and currency at most 1800000 ms apart, are one transfer whatever their merchant and last4: the later gets copy_of the nearest earlier row of the other kind that is live, not held, and has no held or merged copy of the other kind against it. A row without one of these templates takes its role from gates.kind (transfer_notice or account_debit_alert; another value, or a value that is not a string, is dropped). When both rows of a transfer pair say ar pass and sender trusted, the later is merged into the earlier at once (merge_kind transfer, merge_op the ingest op, registered under its dedupe keys) and nobody is asked; txn_copy_resolved keep_both takes it out again, and a null decision merges it again. A pair with an unverified row is held as before. Written by the Swift executor; the ledgerd TypeScript fold (schema 3, removed) and Go (no fold) do not model v4.
format: Each case is a conformance/replay case (log items of ops, expect.state blanked as there, expect.state_sha256 the pass condition), folded by the v4 fold.

cases.name: certain-merge
cases.note: The same alert in two mailboxes shares its Message-ID: one row stays, the other is its alias; neither sender verified, so the earlier import is canonical.

cases.name: verified-wins
cases.note: The later copy's sender verified and the earlier one's did not: the later copy is canonical and the earlier row becomes its alias.

cases.name: reconnect-rescan-no-readd
cases.note: After a reconnect the same message is read again under the same ingest id: it is refused as duplicate_ingest, and the alias list does not grow.

cases.name: probable-hold
cases.note: No shared id; same bank, amount, card and merchant (case and spacing differ) five minutes apart: the second is held as a copy. Eleven minutes apart, or one fils different, stays separate.

cases.name: keep-both
cases.note: The held copy is kept as its own transaction: copy_decision keep_both, counted again.

cases.name: merge-then-undo
cases.note: Merge makes the held copy an alias (merge_kind user); the undo (decision null) brings it back as a held copy, live and indexed again.

cases.name: two-identical-coffees
cases.note: Two real coffees, same card, same amount, three minutes apart, from one mailbox: the second is held, Keep both makes it count, and both stay as two rows; a merge of the kept row with the wrong other row is refused.

cases.name: retire-promotes-the-copy
cases.note: Removing the canonical row's mailbox brings its alias from the other mailbox back as the live row, with the dedupe key; a copy held against the removed row is released.

cases.name: verified-wins-keeps-the-sort
cases.note: The earlier, unverified copy was sorted (txn_categorized, source user) and noted before the verified copy arrived: the verified copy is canonical and takes the sort (category, category_source, needs_review) and the annotations it lacks.

cases.name: retire-promotes-the-sort
cases.note: The canonical row was sorted, then its mailbox was removed: the alias brought back as the live row keeps the sort.

cases.name: merge-retire-keep-both
cases.note: One device merges the held copy, then removes its mailbox, which retires it; another device, offline, chose Keep both on the same copy. The late keep_both is refused with duplicate_disposition_mismatch, and the retired row stays out of the live indexes.

cases.name: edit-on-merged-copy-forwards
cases.note: Another device, offline, sorted and noted the copy that became an alias: the sort and the note reach the canonical row, which had neither.

cases.name: edit-on-merged-copy-keeps-the-canonical-sort
cases.note: The canonical row was already sorted: a late sort of the alias stays on the alias, and the canonical row keeps its own.

cases.name: legacy-categorize-on-v4-row
cases.note: A below-v4 txn_categorized on a v4 row carries no source: the source follows the category (user when set, none when cleared).

cases.name: transfer-notice-holds-its-alert
cases.note: A DIB transfer notice, then the account debit alert for the same transfer three minutes later, with its own merchant and card: the alert is merged into the notice. A same-amount alert two hours later stays its own row.

cases.name: transfer-window
cases.note: A notice and an alert thirty minutes and one second apart stay two rows; another amount's notice and alert exactly thirty minutes apart are one transfer.

cases.name: transfer-alert-then-notice
cases.note: The alert arrives first and the English notice twenty minutes later: the notice is the merged copy.

cases.name: transfer-one-to-one
cases.note: Two same-amount transfers twenty minutes apart, each with its alert, and a third alert: each alert is merged into the nearest notice that has none, the notices never pair with each other, and the third alert stays its own row.

cases.name: transfer-keep-both-then-undo
cases.note: The person says the merged alert is its own movement (keep_both), then undoes that (null): the alert is merged into the notice again.

cases.name: transfer-by-kind-marker
cases.note: Two rows read without a template carry gates.kind transfer_notice and account_debit_alert: they pair as a template pair does. A third row's unknown kind is dropped and it stays its own row.

cases.name: transfer-unverified-held
cases.note: The notice's sender did not verify: its alert is held as its copy for the person, as before.
